items.stem: In Oracle, what is the difference between an instance and a database?

options.text: The instance is memory and processes; the database is the files on disk
options.rationale: Correct: the instance (SGA + background processes) accesses the database's physical files.

options.text: The database is memory; the instance is the files
The instance stores all table data permanently
options.rationale: Persistent data lives in the database files, not the instance memory.

items.stem: Which principle should guide granting database privileges?

options.text: Least privilege — grant only what is needed
options.rationale: Correct: least privilege limits risk from misuse or compromise.

options.text: Grant DBA to all developers for convenience

options.rationale: Granting to PUBLIC exposes privileges to everyone.

items.explanation: Correct: least privilege limits risk from misuse or compromise.

items.stem: Which TWO make a backup strategy trustworthy?

options.text: Regularly testing a restore from the backups
options.rationale: Correct: an untested backup may not be recoverable.

options.text: Storing a copy in a separate location
options.rationale: Correct: off-site/separate copies survive local failures.

options.text: Keeping backups only on the same disk as the database
options.rationale: Co-located backups are lost with the disk.

options.text: Disabling archive logging on a production OLTP database

items.explanation: Correct: an untested backup may not be recoverable.
